claims.text: Multilayer electrospark deposition using SPS-manufactured alloy electrodes can produce a sound, crack-resistant repair in materials that are difficult to repair by fusion welding.
Such a repair can enable continued service of the damaged component under aggressive operating conditions.
The component's microstructural features make it prone to hot cracking during traditional fusion-welding repair.
Elevated temperature and mechanical loading exacerbate hot cracking in fusion-welded repairs.
The proposed process produces a multilayered, metallurgically bonded deposited layer.
The deposited layer has a refined grain structure.
The deposited layer has diminished residual stress.
Refined grains and diminished residual stress minimize hot-crack formation.
Spark plasma sintering produces dense alloy electrodes.
Spark plasma sintering produces homogenized alloy electrodes.
Electrospark deposition has lower thermal input than traditional fusion-welding repair.
Reduced thermal input minimizes localized overheating and hot cracking.
Electrospark deposition using SPS-prepared electrodes ensures strong bonding to the substrate.
The proposed repair will produce fewer or no hot cracks than traditional fusion-welding repair under similar aggressive operating conditions.
The proposed repair will have improved mechanical integrity relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
Traditional fusion-welding repair is prone to hot cracking because of excessive localized heat.
Unsuitable microstructural evolution during traditional fusion welding contributes to hot cracking.
The magnitude of improvement and long-term durability may vary with alloy composition, deposition parameters, and service conditions.
